results: 1. Measure palpebral fissure height in both eyes
lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides): MRD1 raised on the LEFT (retraction); right lid height normal - the right eye is NOT ptotic
2. Measure levator function in both eyes (using a millimeter ruler)
3. Check both pupils for size and reaction to light
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
4. Assess full extraocular movements in all directions of gaze
ocular motility examination: full in all directions
5. Perform a fatigue test (sustained upgaze for 2 minutes) on the ptotic eyelid
sustained upgaze fatigability test: no fatigable droop
6. Perform an ice test on the ptotic eyelid
7. Perform a phenylephrine drop test on the ptotic eyelid
8. If no clear cause is established, MRI brain and orbits with contrast
MRI orbits: no extraocular muscle enlargement, no mass
MRI brain with contrast: no dorsal midbrain lesion - excludes Collier sign
dx_raw:
**DIAGNOSIS:** Compensatory left upper eyelid retraction (Hering's law) secondary to right upper eyelid ptosis, most likely aponeurotic dehiscence of the levator

**Alternatives:**
1. Mild/early thyroid eye disease presenting with isolated unilateral lid retraction
2. Congenital right upper lid ptosis with long-standing compensatory left retraction
3. Idiopathic/benign unilateral eyelid retraction with incidental history of contralateral ptosis
